target: Standalone Android reconstruction; Windows native addresses are reference evidence only.

portable_boundary.dispatch: Namespace and method name, backed by explicit provider implementations. Never dispatch by original x86 addresses.
portable_boundary.receiver: Provider receiver belongs to the host implementation; reconstructed Lua arguments exclude an automatically inserted self. Native closure upvalue0 supplies receiver in inspected wrappers.
portable_boundary.argument_and_result_lists: Preserve order, explicit length, trailing nil, multiple results and errors. Do not coerce according to guessed signatures.
portable_boundary.handles: Opaque identity tokens backed by two uint32 words or canonical16-hex text; shared interning per Lua realm. Domain and key are not a Lua number. Key existence and lifetime belong to the engine implementation.
portable_boundary.strings: Preserve Lua byte strings and length; do not assume all data is UTF-8 or null-terminated at the portable API boundary.
portable_boundary.numbers: Keep reconstructed VM numeric semantics explicit; native tests currently cover bounded signed32-bit domains. Do not substitute host floating-point behavior for verified integer rules.
portable_boundary.missing_features: Return explicit unimplemented errors through the provider layer; do not fabricate empty worlds, false query results, successful quest transitions or missing-handle defaults.
portable_boundary.native_state: No original lua_State layout, engine context offset, GC header, vtable or calling convention crosses the portable boundary.

provider_domains.QUEST: Quest key resolution, state/stage transitions and notifications require explicit engine contracts.
provider_domains.ACTOR: Entity identity/lifetime and world actions require explicit engine contracts.
provider_domains.TIME: Timers require an explicit clock/tick model; registered names alone do not establish time units or pause behavior.
provider_domains.GAME: World/space readiness and lifecycle require explicit engine contracts.
provider_domains.WINDOW: UI object ownership and widget behavior require explicit engine contracts; rendering may use Android implementation.
